facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against the benign reading is that it rests on a sharp earnings step-up: the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.0% in Q3 2026 against 20.0% in Q3 2025, and the AA&S segment's EBITDA of USD 181.3 million in Q3 2026 was about double the USD 90.4 million of a year earlier, so the trailing denominator contains an unusually strong quarter. Working capital absorbed USD 255.1 million into inventories in 9M 2026, and shareholder returns exceeded free cash flow in that period. The view would weaken if net debt keeps rising while reported EBITDA stalls, if inventory build is not matched by shipments, or if the USD 425 million repurchase authorisation is funded from the revolving facility. It would strengthen if cash interest for the nine months is disclosed and confirms cover near the annual level, or if shareholder returns fall back within free cash flow. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50; calculation C16

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Business risk is concentrated in aerospace and defense but backed by contracts. The sector was about 68% of FY2025 sales and 69% of Q3 2026 sales, with commercial jet engines at 42% of Q3 2026 sales; about 92% of High Performance Materials & Components revenue and 41% of Advanced Alloys & Solutions revenue come from it. Most major engine and airframe makers have long-term agreements with the company, no customer exceeded 10% of sales, and confirmed orders were about USD 3.7 billion at 2025-12-28, of which about 70% were due to ship in FY2026. For creditors that means a year of covered volume against a cycle the company itself calls hard to predict. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Growth is strong and driven by volume and pricing, which supports near-term cash flow, but one segment's quarterly margin eased. Sales rose 26.49% in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 and 12.49% over 9M 2026; Advanced Alloys & Solutions earned segment EBITDA of USD 181.3 million against USD 90.4 million, while High Performance Materials & Components earned USD 167.3 million against USD 145.8 million and its quarterly margin eased to 23.2% from 24.2% on the cost of moving a new nickel-based superalloy into production, although its nine-month margin rose to 24.0% from 23.4%. That cost is the main operating item to watch because the engine-component segment carries most of the growth case. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Ownership does not read as a sponsor story, but it is not established. The company has a broad record-holder base, pays no dividend, and the filings read name no controlling or large holder; holdings above reporting thresholds, board composition and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. The only named outside owner is China Baowu Steel Group with 40% of the Chinese strip joint venture, whose cash and dividends belong partly to that minority. The consequence is no evidence of sponsor extraction or support in either direction, and payout risk comes from the board and public holders rather than a financial owner. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Financial policy is mixed: debt is refinanced early and lengthened, but cash goes to buybacks faster than it is generated. In 2026 the company issued USD 450.0 million of 2033 notes and redeemed USD 350.0 million of 2027 notes ahead of maturity, which removes the nearest maturity, yet treasury stock purchases were USD 470.0 million in FY2025, 140.85% of free cash flow of USD 333.7 million, and USD 195.0 million in 9M 2026, 98.48% of free cash flow. The credit facility sets no limit on dividends while undrawn availability stays above the greater of USD 120 million and 20% of the facility, and the filings do not say whether repurchases face the same test, so creditor protection rests on that availability and on board policy. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a stable reading is concentration and cyclicality: the company says commercial aerospace has been cyclical and hard to predict, confirmed orders fell to about USD 3.7 billion from about USD 3.9 billion while sales rose, about 35% of the workforce is under collective agreements, international sales were about 42% of FY2025 sales and nickel hedges cover only about 7% of a year's purchases, so trade policy and metal prices can hit margins faster than surcharges recover them. Buybacks that exceed free cash flow add to this by keeping net debt from falling when earnings are strong. The view would weaken if engine build rates or the order backlog fall, if the quarterly margin of the engine-component segment keeps easing, or if buybacks are funded from the revolving facility. It would strengthen if the proxy statement shows no dominant holder with payout influence, or if the board caps payouts at free cash flow. facts.text: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against an improving reading is that the fall in leverage rests on one earnings step-up concentrated in one quarter and one segment: Advanced Alloys & Solutions segment EBITDA of USD 181.3 million in Q3 2026 was about double the USD 90.4 million of a year earlier, net debt did not fall, and shareholder returns exceeded free cash flow. If earnings fell back to the FY2025 level with debt unchanged, total debt over reported EBITDA would be 2.35x and net debt 1.79x, above the 1.92x and 1.46x reported now, and 2.49x and 1.90x at the FY2024 level. Revenue growth of 9.29% over FY2025 produced EBITDA growth of 22.75%, so operating leverage works in both directions. The evidence for the view is that backlog is above its level of a year earlier and liquidity covers the next maturity 3.11 times, so a fall to the FY2025 or FY2024 earnings level would raise leverage but not threaten liquidity. The view would weaken if confirmed orders fall below USD 4.3 billion, if the engine-component margin keeps easing, if free cash flow stays below shareholder returns, or if buybacks are funded from the revolving facility. It would strengthen if free cash flow covers shareholder returns and net debt starts to fall while EBITDA holds. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is cyclical, concentrated by end market but not by customer, and covered by contracts for about a year. Volume, price and mix drove growth of 26.49% in Q3 2026, led by commercial jet engine products, and about 75% of the USD 4.3 billion backlog is due within the next 12 months. Most products are sold under contracts with raw material surcharges and index mechanisms, which pass metal prices through, but the annual report states that long-term contracts can be renegotiated or re-priced at intervals and that excess capacity and competition have at times cut prices excluding surcharges. The credit implication is predictable revenue in the near term with re-pricing risk at renewals and cyclical risk beyond the order book. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure but not under a build-rate shock combined with input cost inflation. Last-twelve-months revenue grew 9.29% over FY2025 while reported EBITDA grew 22.75%, which shows strong operating leverage on the way up and the same leverage on the way down. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next year or two the tailwinds are the order book of about USD 4.3 billion, price and mix gains, defense and specialty energy growth in the alloy segment, and a refinancing that has removed nearby maturities; these support revenue, margin and cash-flow visibility. The headwinds are superalloy ramp costs, inventory build, tariff and input cost exposure and payouts above free cash flow, which pressure margin, free cash flow and deleveraging. Over three to five years the credit depends on whether the earnings step-up lasts through the FY2029 and FY2030 maturities of USD 325.0 million of senior notes and USD 633.4 million in the largest ladder year, and on whether the company keeps returns within free cash flow as capacity growth ends. citations.quote: Over the next year or two the tailwinds are the order book of about USD 4.3 billion, price and mix gains, defense and specialty energy growth in the alloy segment, and a refinancing that has removed nearby maturities; these support revenue, margin and cash-flow visibility. The headwinds are superalloy ramp costs, inventory build, tariff and input cost exposure and payouts above free cash flow, which pressure margin, free cash flow and deleveraging. Over three to five years the credit depends on whether the earnings step-up lasts through the FY2029 and FY2030 maturities of USD 325.0 million of senior notes and USD 633.4 million in the largest ladder year, and on whether the company keeps returns within free cash flow as capacity growth ends.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 43; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The realistic downside starts with a cut in commercial engine build rates or a trade shock that raises nickel and titanium costs ahead of surcharges. The first operating break is lower engine-component volume and a margin squeeze from fixed labour and superalloy ramp costs, with inventories, already up USD 255.1 million in 9M 2026, slow to unwind. Because EBITDA grew 22.75% on revenue growth of 9.29%, a reversal would cut EBITDA faster than revenue: at the FY2025 level of USD 789.0 million, with debt unchanged, total debt over EBITDA would be 2.35x and net debt 1.79x, and at the FY2024 level of USD 745.8 million, 2.49x and 1.90x. Cash flow would fall with EBITDA, and if buybacks continued free cash flow would again sit below returns. Management can slow growth capex, stop buybacks, which are discretionary, and release inventory. Liquidity of USD 1,012.3 million would still cover the USD 325.0 million FY2029 maturity 3.11 times, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, but leverage would return to the levels of FY2024 and FY2025 and refinancing in FY2029 and FY2030 would be harder if the market had turned. The signals to watch are orders, the Adjusted EBITDA margin, free cash flow against returns and availability under the revolver. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Ati Inc presents an adequate business profile supported by qualified aerospace products, contract cover for about a year and USD 1,012.3 million of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by shareholder returns above free cash flow, concentration in the aerospace cycle and USD 203.0 million of funding outside reported debt. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: free cash flow is positive in every period but absorbs growth investment, and free cash flow after returns was negative in 9M 2026. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding earnings through FY2029 and FY2030, when USD 325.0 million of senior notes and the largest ladder year of USD 633.4 million fall due. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector the profile cannot be placed because peer data is not supplied. The primary downside path is a fall in engine build rates while buybacks continue, which would lift leverage back toward 2.35x. Further analysis would require agency ratings, the executed credit agreement and indentures, peer data and the proxy statement. Top risk: earnings concentrated in the commercial aerospace cycle combined with shareholder returns above free cash flow. # Ati Inc financial foundation
## Request

Financial foundation for Ati Inc (ati-1018963), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, net debt, leverage, cash interest cover, liquidity and the debt stack in USD millions for FY2024, FY2025 and the periods to 2026-09-27.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-29_ati_ati-20241229.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 2024-12-29, audited | 2025-02-21 | 5129255a626b98f7addfdf609eb74e55b220dc6812a97d8d2e664b25268101e0 | FY2024 as first reported; FY2024 interest paid, liquidity and leverage reconciliation |

| 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 2025-12-28, audited | 2026-02-20 | 5d347abcfa7f23bf17cce990198026c6f76789751d8e82391f3d73b8889e6812 | FY2025 and FY2024 statements, debt note, EBITDA reconciliation, maturity schedule, funding float and subsequent event |

## Findings
### Bottom line

Ati Inc has deleveraged to 1.92x total debt and 1.46x net debt on reported EBITDA at 2026-09-27 and holds USD 1,012.3 million of liquidity, so creditors face low refinancing risk, with shareholder returns and inventory growth the main drains on that headroom.
Basis: calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C35; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 2

Reported EBITDA rose from USD 745.8 million in FY2024 to USD 789.0 million in FY2025 and USD 968.5 million over the last twelve months. The 2033 notes of USD 450.0 million refinanced the 2027 notes, so the next maturity is USD 325.0 million in FY2029. Interest cover was 6.70x in FY2025 and cannot be calculated for the last twelve months, because cash interest is printed only in annual reports.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C27; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 47
### Key findings

Total debt to reported EBITDA fell from 2.54x at FY2024 to 2.22x at FY2025 and 1.92x on the last twelve months to 2026-09-27, but net debt to reported EBITDA moved from 1.57x to 1.69x and then to 1.46x. In FY2025 the fall in gross debt was paid for with cash: the company repaid USD 150.0 million of debentures and repurchased USD 470.0 million of stock, so cash fell by USD 304.5 million and net debt rose from USD 1,174.1 million to USD 1,332.7 million. Since then the improvement is earnings-led, because net debt rose again to USD 1,415.2 million while reported EBITDA grew to USD 968.5 million.

Basis: calculation C17; calculation C23; calculation C29; calculation C18; calculation C24; calculation C30; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 101

Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 5.68x in FY2024 and 6.70x in FY2025, on interest and commitment fees paid of USD 131.4 million and USD 117.8 million. The quarterly reports do not print cash interest, so cover for the last twelve months is not established. Net interest expense was USD 70.2 million in 9M 2026 against USD 74.5 million a year earlier, which suggests cover has not weakened, but that is an analyst inference from expense and not a measured cash figure.
Basis: calculation C21; calculation C27; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

Cash from operating activities was USD 414.6 million in 9M 2026 against USD 298.5 million in 9M 2025, but USD 255.1 million went into inventories, against USD 57.5 million a year earlier, as the company built stock seasonally and for higher operating levels. After capital expenditures of USD 216.6 million, free cash flow was USD 198.0 million in 9M 2026 and USD 421.1 million over the last twelve months, which is 43.48% of reported EBITDA. Shareholder returns of USD 277.2 million in 9M 2026, made up of USD 195.0 million of buybacks and USD 82.2 million of shares withheld for tax, exceeded free cash flow by USD 79.2 million, which explains most of the rise in net debt.
Basis: calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C57; calculation C15; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 45

Liquidity at 2026-09-27 was USD 1,012.3 million: USD 442.3 million of cash, of which USD 106.1 million is held by the 60%-owned Chinese joint venture, and about USD 570 million undrawn under the asset-based revolving facility after USD 29.3 million of letters of credit. Liquidity was USD 985.7 million at FY2025 and USD 1,246.2 million at FY2024. The facility carries a fixed charge coverage covenant of at least 1.00x, tested only if availability falls below the greater of 10% of the facility and USD 60.0 million, and requires minimum liquidity in the 90 days before the 2029, 2030 and 2031 notes mature; the issuer reports compliance with the coverage ratio, but headroom is not calculable because the covenant definitions and the liquidity level are not supplied.

Basis: calculation C35; calculation C34; calculation C33; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 47

Debt at 2026-09-27 is USD 1,857.5 million at carrying value and USD 1,872.7 million at principal: four series of senior notes totalling USD 1,550.0 million, a USD 200.0 million secured term loan under the asset-based facility, USD 107.1 million of finance leases and other, and USD 15.6 million drawn on foreign credit facilities. The USD 450.0 million 2033 notes issued on 2026-06-03 funded the USD 350.0 million redemption of the 2027 notes on 2026-07-08, so the next maturity is the USD 325.0 million 2029 senior notes in the fourth quarter of FY2029, and the term loan falls due in June 2030. The only maturity ladder printed is at FY2025, where FY2030 is the largest year at USD 633.4 million.

Basis: calculation C40; calculation C42; calculation C41; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 102

Funding that sits outside reported debt is growing. Supplier financing in accounts payable rose from USD 52.8 million at 2025-12-28 to USD 83.0 million at 2026-09-27; customers' receivable-sale programmes took USD 377.5 million of invoices in 9M 2026 against USD 271.1 million a year earlier; USD 120 million of the USD 125.0 million receivables facility is used; and contract liabilities, which are amounts customers have been billed ahead of delivery, total USD 273.2 million against USD 237.7 million at the start of the year. If banks or customers withdrew these programmes, working capital would absorb cash and net leverage would be higher than reported.
Basis: calculation C62; calculation C63; calculation C64; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13

The issuer's own leverage ratios, 1.74x total debt and 1.33x net debt at 2026-09-27, are lower than the 1.92x and 1.46x above because the issuer divides by trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,075.9 million, an effect that outweighs its use of higher principal debt. Adjusted EBITDA exceeds reported EBITDA by USD 107.4 million over the last twelve months, of which restructuring and other charges are USD 87.3 million, against USD 22.1 million in FY2024 and USD 48.8 million in FY2025. Because these charges recur and are growing, reported EBITDA is the safer denominator.

Basis: calculation C60; calculation C72; calculation C73; calculation C61; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 63

No financing, acquisition, disposal or dividend after the 2026-09-27 balance sheet is stated. The one subsequent event in the annual report is the board's authorisation on 2026-02-18 of up to USD 500.0 million of further share repurchases; USD 425 million of authorisation remained at 2026-09-27, so capacity for shareholder returns that compete with creditors for cash remains.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 142; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against the benign reading is that it rests on a sharp earnings step-up: the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.0% in Q3 2026 against 20.0% in Q3 2025, and the AA&S segment's EBITDA of USD 181.3 million in Q3 2026 was about double the USD 90.4 million of a year earlier, so the trailing denominator contains an unusually strong quarter. Working capital absorbed USD 255.1 million into inventories in 9M 2026, and shareholder returns exceeded free cash flow in that period. The view would weaken if net debt keeps rising while reported EBITDA stalls, if inventory build is not matched by shipments, or if the USD 425 million repurchase authorisation is funded from the revolving facility. It would strengthen if cash interest for the nine months is disclosed and confirms cover near the annual level, or if shareholder returns fall back within free cash flow.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50; calculation C16
### Limitations
- Cash interest paid is not printed in the quarterly reports, so interest cover for the last twelve months is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4
- The maturity ladder is drawn at 2025-12-28 and is stale for 2026-09-27: it still includes the 2027 notes and omits the 2033 notes.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 15

- No executed credit agreement or indenture is supplied, so the rank and security of the 2029 and 2031 senior notes, guarantor scope and the covenant definitions are not established, and the debt stack lists only facilities whose rank the filings state.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16
- The last twelve months figures combine audited annual figures with unaudited interim figures, and undrawn revolving capacity is the issuer's approximate figure, not a borrowing base calculation.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 50

# Ati Inc business, ownership and transactions
## Request

Business, ownership, governance and transaction facts for Ati Inc (ati-1018963), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business and operating model, ownership and control, capital allocation behaviour, and the transactions and events from FY2024 to 2026-09-27.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Ati Inc is a technically qualified but end-market-concentrated aerospace and defense materials supplier, with large-holder ownership not established and buybacks as the main way cash leaves the company, so creditors depend on engine demand and board restraint on payouts.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 76

Aerospace and defense is about 68% of sales and commercial jet engines alone were 42% of sales in Q3 2026, but long-term agreements, confirmed orders of about USD 3.7 billion and no customer above 10% of sales give visibility. Treasury stock purchases of USD 470.0 million in FY2025 were 140.85% of free cash flow, and no dividend is paid.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation C4; calculation C7
### Key findings

Business risk is concentrated in aerospace and defense but backed by contracts. The sector was about 68% of FY2025 sales and 69% of Q3 2026 sales, with commercial jet engines at 42% of Q3 2026 sales; about 92% of High Performance Materials & Components revenue and 41% of Advanced Alloys & Solutions revenue come from it. Most major engine and airframe makers have long-term agreements with the company, no customer exceeded 10% of sales, and confirmed orders were about USD 3.7 billion at 2025-12-28, of which about 70% were due to ship in FY2026. For creditors that means a year of covered volume against a cycle the company itself calls hard to predict.

Growth is strong and driven by volume and pricing, which supports near-term cash flow, but one segment's quarterly margin eased. Sales rose 26.49% in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 and 12.49% over 9M 2026; Advanced Alloys & Solutions earned segment EBITDA of USD 181.3 million against USD 90.4 million, while High Performance Materials & Components earned USD 167.3 million against USD 145.8 million and its quarterly margin eased to 23.2% from 24.2% on the cost of moving a new nickel-based superalloy into production, although its nine-month margin rose to 24.0% from 23.4%. That cost is the main operating item to watch because the engine-component segment carries most of the growth case.

Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 43

Ownership does not read as a sponsor story, but it is not established. The company has a broad record-holder base, pays no dividend, and the filings read name no controlling or large holder; holdings above reporting thresholds, board composition and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. The only named outside owner is China Baowu Steel Group with 40% of the Chinese strip joint venture, whose cash and dividends belong partly to that minority. The consequence is no evidence of sponsor extraction or support in either direction, and payout risk comes from the board and public holders rather than a financial owner.

Financial policy is mixed: debt is refinanced early and lengthened, but cash goes to buybacks faster than it is generated. In 2026 the company issued USD 450.0 million of 2033 notes and redeemed USD 350.0 million of 2027 notes ahead of maturity, which removes the nearest maturity, yet treasury stock purchases were USD 470.0 million in FY2025, 140.85% of free cash flow of USD 333.7 million, and USD 195.0 million in 9M 2026, 98.48% of free cash flow. The credit facility sets no limit on dividends while undrawn availability stays above the greater of USD 120 million and 20% of the facility, and the filings do not say whether repurchases face the same test, so creditor protection rests on that availability and on board policy.

Basis: calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C4; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 123–124; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

Capital spending is rising to fund aerospace growth, and it competes with debt reduction for cash. Capital expenditures were USD 239.1 million in FY2024, USD 280.6 million in FY2025 and USD 216.6 million in 9M 2026 against USD 187.9 million in 9M 2025, mainly growth projects, and restructuring and transformation charges recur. Free cash flow after this spending, not EBITDA, is what is available for debt reduction.

Claims outside debt are modest against earnings but not zero. Pension and retiree benefit liabilities were USD 187.9 million at 2026-09-27, environmental reserves are about USD 15 million with up to USD 21 million more reasonably possible, and a pension class action over the 2023 annuity purchase is pending with a recommendation to dismiss. These claims sit outside reported debt and would matter mainly in a downturn.
Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a stable reading is concentration and cyclicality: the company says commercial aerospace has been cyclical and hard to predict, confirmed orders fell to about USD 3.7 billion from about USD 3.9 billion while sales rose, about 35% of the workforce is under collective agreements, international sales were about 42% of FY2025 sales and nickel hedges cover only about 7% of a year's purchases, so trade policy and metal prices can hit margins faster than surcharges recover them. Buybacks that exceed free cash flow add to this by keeping net debt from falling when earnings are strong. The view would weaken if engine build rates or the order backlog fall, if the quarterly margin of the engine-component segment keeps easing, or if buybacks are funded from the revolving facility. It would strengthen if the proxy statement shows no dominant holder with payout influence, or if the board caps payouts at free cash flow.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C7; calculation C8
### Limitations

- Large-holder ownership, board composition and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the conclusion that no financial owner extracts value rests on missing evidence and would change if a dominant holder is found.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 149–150

- No executed credit agreement or indenture is supplied, so the statement that dividends are limited only by an availability test rests on the filing's own summary and could change with the document's definitions, including whether repurchases are covered.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 123–124

- Customer names beyond the engine and airframe makers the filing lists, contract tenors and re-pricing dates are not disclosed, so the visibility that long-term agreements give cannot be measured beyond the backlog.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 78
- Quarterly growth and margin figures are unaudited, so the conclusion that growth is strong and driven by volume and pricing could change when the year-end audit is complete.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 39–43

The refinancing added no secured debt and moved the next maturity to the fourth quarter of FY2029.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 47

A receivables facility of up to USD 125.0 million, entered on 2025-09-19, had USD 120 million of funding used at 2026-09-27; receivables sold under it leave the balance sheet and so sit outside reported debt.

No acquisition is described in the filings for FY2024 to 9M 2026. The transactions that moved cash were debt repayment and refinancing, small disposals and share repurchases, with USD 425 million of repurchase authority remaining at 2026-09-27.

# Ati Inc fundamental credit view
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Ati Inc (ati-1018963), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, financial and ownership profile, ranked strengths and weaknesses, a downside path and monitoring triggers, built from the five filings and the findings of Source readiness, Business & governance and Financial foundation.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Ati Inc's credit profile is improving, with total debt at 1.92x and net debt at 1.46x reported EBITDA and USD 1,012.3 million of liquidity, so near-term refinancing risk is low, but shareholder returns exceed free cash flow, so deleveraging relies on earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C9

Aerospace and defense is about 68% of sales and commercial jet engines were 42% of Q3 2026 sales, so one cycle drives cash flow, though long-term agreements and confirmed orders of about USD 4.3 billion cover about a year. The nearest senior note maturity is USD 325.0 million in FY2029, which liquidity covers 3.11 times, and net debt rose by USD 82.5 million since FY2025 while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 968.5 million is 22.75% above FY2025.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 36; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3
### Key findings

Leverage is falling because earnings are rising, not because debt is being repaid. Total debt over reported EBITDA fell from 2.54x at FY2024 to 2.22x at FY2025 and 1.92x on the last twelve months, but net debt rose from USD 1,332.7 million at FY2025 to USD 1,415.2 million at 2026-09-27, so the gain came from last-twelve-months reported EBITDA reaching USD 968.5 million, not from paydown. On FY2025 EBITDA of USD 789.0 million the same debt would be 2.35x total and 1.79x net, and on the lower FY2024 EBITDA of USD 745.8 million it would be 2.49x and 1.90x, so the ratios depend on the earnings step-up holding.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8

Liquidity and maturities are the strongest part of the credit. Liquidity of USD 1,012.3 million, made of USD 442.3 million of cash and about USD 570 million of undrawn revolving capacity, covers the next senior note maturity of USD 325.0 million, due in the fourth quarter of FY2029, 3.11 times, and the 2026 refinancing replaced the USD 350.0 million of 2027 notes with USD 450.0 million of unsecured 2033 notes. The only maturity ladder printed predates that refinancing and shows FY2030 as the largest year at USD 633.4 million, consistent with the 2030 notes and the asset-based term loan falling due together, so the test of market access sits in FY2029 and FY2030, not before.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C1

Free cash flow is real but is being fully distributed. Free cash flow was USD 333.7 million in FY2025 and USD 198.0 million in 9M 2026, USD 421.1 million over the last twelve months or 43.48% of reported EBITDA, after inventories absorbed USD 255.1 million and capital expenditures were USD 216.6 million in 9M 2026. Shareholder returns of USD 277.2 million in the same nine months exceeded free cash flow by USD 79.2 million, and treasury stock purchases were 140.85% of free cash flow in FY2025, so cash that could have repaid debt went to holders and net debt rose.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C10

Revenue visibility is good for about a year and improving. Confirmed orders were about USD 4.3 billion at 2026-09-27 against about USD 3.6 billion a year earlier, and about 75% of them are due to be satisfied within the next 12 months; most major engine and airframe makers hold long-term agreements with the company, and no customer exceeded 10% of sales. This supersedes the year-end reading in Business & governance that orders fell from about USD 3.9 billion to about USD 3.7 billion, because the interim figure is later and shows growth over the year, although the backlog eased slightly from about USD 4.4 billion at 2026-06-28.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-28_ati_ati-20260628.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 11; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Business risk rests on one cycle. Aerospace and defense was about 68% of FY2025 sales and commercial jet engines alone were 42% of Q3 2026 sales, and commercial jet engines were 74% of the engine-component segment's Q3 2026 sales; the annual report calls the commercial aerospace cycle hard to predict, so a fall in engine build rates would reach revenue, margin and cash flow together, and other markets at 31% of Q3 2026 sales soften that only partly.

Margins are improving on volume, price and mix, but the gain is concentrated in one segment and exposed to input costs. The issuer's Adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.0% in Q3 2026 against 20.0% a year earlier, and Advanced Alloys & Solutions earned segment EBITDA of USD 181.3 million against USD 90.4 million, a margin of 25.8% against 17.3%, while the High Performance Materials & Components margin eased to 23.2% from 24.2% on the cost of moving a new superalloy into production. Raw material surcharges pass most nickel and titanium moves through, but hedges cover only about 7% of a year's nickel purchases, so tariffs and delays can hit margin before recovery.

Funding outside reported debt flatters leverage. Supplier financing of USD 83.0 million and USD 120 million used under the receivables facility total USD 203.0 million, 14.34% of net debt, and customers' receivable programmes took USD 377.5 million of invoices in 9M 2026. If banks or customers withdrew these programmes, working capital would absorb cash and net leverage would be higher than reported.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13; calculation C14

Financial policy is the weakest dimension. The company pays no dividend but has USD 425 million of repurchase authority left, the asset-based facility sets no dividend limit while undrawn availability stays above the greater of USD 120 million and 20% of the facility, and the nearest senior note maturity is far enough away that buybacks can continue without an immediate refinancing constraint. Holders above reporting thresholds are not established, so no controlling owner is identified to weigh either way; the 60%-owned Chinese joint venture holds USD 106.1 million of the cash, which is not wholly available to creditors of the parent.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 123–124; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against an improving reading is that the fall in leverage rests on one earnings step-up concentrated in one quarter and one segment: Advanced Alloys & Solutions segment EBITDA of USD 181.3 million in Q3 2026 was about double the USD 90.4 million of a year earlier, net debt did not fall, and shareholder returns exceeded free cash flow. If earnings fell back to the FY2025 level with debt unchanged, total debt over reported EBITDA would be 2.35x and net debt 1.79x, above the 1.92x and 1.46x reported now, and 2.49x and 1.90x at the FY2024 level. Revenue growth of 9.29% over FY2025 produced EBITDA growth of 22.75%, so operating leverage works in both directions. The evidence for the view is that backlog is above its level of a year earlier and liquidity covers the next maturity 3.11 times, so a fall to the FY2025 or FY2024 earnings level would raise leverage but not threaten liquidity. The view would weaken if confirmed orders fall below USD 4.3 billion, if the engine-component margin keeps easing, if free cash flow stays below shareholder returns, or if buybacks are funded from the revolving facility. It would strengthen if free cash flow covers shareholder returns and net debt starts to fall while EBITDA holds.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 43; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8
### Limitations

- Agency ratings, bond prices and spreads are not supplied, so the judgement that refinancing risk is low through FY2028 rests on liquidity and maturity timing alone and would change if the market priced the notes as stressed.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- No peer financial data is supplied, so the comparison of this profile with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is qualitative and the profile could rank higher or lower against an actual peer set.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so guarantor scope, lien rank of the senior notes and restricted-payment baskets are the analyst's reading of the filings' summaries, and the conclusion that payouts are limited only by an availability test could change with the documents' definitions.

- The downside scenario is qualitative: no management forecast, build-rate guidance or agency downgrade threshold is supplied, so the size of each step is an illustration from earlier reported earnings, and the conclusion that liquidity survives it could change if working capital or margins behave differently.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C7

- Backlog is reported in billions to one decimal at a single date, and the share due within 12 months is approximate, so the conclusion that revenue is covered for about a year could change if orders convert more slowly.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 7
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is the earnings-led fall in leverage: last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 968.5 million puts total debt at 1.92x and net debt at 1.46x, so interest cover and refinancing capacity improve for as long as earnings hold, and the issuer's own ratios of 1.74x and 1.33x on Adjusted EBITDA point the same way.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3

The second strength is the liquidity and maturity runway: USD 1,012.3 million of liquidity covers the next senior note maturity of USD 325.0 million 3.11 times, so no refinancing is needed before FY2029 and the company can fund working capital and capacity growth from cash and the revolver.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

The third strength is contract cover: long-term agreements with most major aerospace makers, no customer above 10% of sales and orders of about USD 4.3 billion, about 75% of them due within the next 12 months, fix volume for about a year and steady the cash flow that services debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 9; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The first weakness is shareholder returns above free cash flow: USD 277.2 million of returns against USD 198.0 million of free cash flow in 9M 2026, leave a gap of USD 79.2 million, so net debt rises even as EBITDA grows and leverage falls only if earnings keep rising.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C9; calculation C10

The second weakness is concentration in one cycle: about 68% of FY2025 sales are aerospace and defense, so a downturn in engine build rates would cut EBITDA and lift leverage together, and the company's own statement that the cycle is hard to predict leaves no basis for assuming it away.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 17; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The third weakness is funding outside reported debt: supplier financing and receivables facility funding of USD 203.0 million equal 14.34% of net debt and could reverse, which would raise net leverage above the reported 1.46x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13; calculation C14

### Company description and credit linkage

ATI Inc. makes specialty materials and components, mainly nickel-based alloys and superalloys, titanium alloys and zirconium, hafnium and niobium products, in two segments of similar size: High Performance Materials & Components, which sells engine and airframe parts mostly under multi-year agreements, and Advanced Alloys & Solutions, which sells flat-rolled products into aerospace, energy, automotive and electronics markets. Qualified products and long-term agreements support visibility of cash flow, so debt service capacity is good while the cycle holds; the concentration in commercial aerospace means a cyclical decline would reach both segments, and the year of covered orders limits how fast it would show in cash flow and liquidity.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 9
### Ownership and group structure

The common stock is listed and widely held, no controlling or large holder is named in the filings read, and holders above reporting thresholds, board composition and related-party dealings are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied. The only named outside owner is China Baowu Steel Group with 40% of the Chinese strip joint venture, which the company controls with 60% and consolidates, and that joint venture's USD 106.1 million of cash sits inside consolidated cash. The issuer is ATI Inc. itself; guarantors of the notes are not stated. The credit consequence is no evidence of sponsor extraction or support, with payout behaviour set by the board's repurchase decisions.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 10; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is cyclical, concentrated by end market but not by customer, and covered by contracts for about a year. Volume, price and mix drove growth of 26.49% in Q3 2026, led by commercial jet engine products, and about 75% of the USD 4.3 billion backlog is due within the next 12 months. Most products are sold under contracts with raw material surcharges and index mechanisms, which pass metal prices through, but the annual report states that long-term contracts can be renegotiated or re-priced at intervals and that excess capacity and competition have at times cut prices excluding surcharges. The credit implication is predictable revenue in the near term with re-pricing risk at renewals and cyclical risk beyond the order book.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure but not under a build-rate shock combined with input cost inflation. Last-twelve-months revenue grew 9.29% over FY2025 while reported EBITDA grew 22.75%, which shows strong operating leverage on the way up and the same leverage on the way down. About 35% of the workforce is covered by collective bargaining agreements, nickel hedges cover only about 7% of a year's purchases, and the engine-component segment margin eased in Q3 2026 on superalloy ramp costs, so fixed labour and ramp costs could outrun surcharges in a downturn; the split of fixed and variable costs is not stated.

### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Free cash flow conversion is moderate and absorbs growth investment, so EBITDA does not translate fully into cash for debt service. Free cash flow was 42.29% of reported EBITDA in FY2025 and 25.44% in 9M 2026, when inventories took USD 255.1 million, and 43.48% over the last twelve months. Capital expenditures were USD 239.1 million in FY2024, USD 280.6 million in FY2025 and USD 216.6 million in 9M 2026, mainly growth projects the company can slow, so capex is flexible; interest and commitment fees paid were USD 117.8 million in FY2025, and the split of maintenance and growth capex is not stated. The implication is that debt reduction depends on free cash flow after returns, which was negative in 9M 2026.

### Porter's five forces

Competitive rivalry is moderate in qualified aerospace products and higher in flat-rolled industrial products. The annual report names Precision Castparts under Berkshire Hathaway, Howmet Aerospace, Carpenter Technology and Aubert & Duval as principal competitors of the engine-component segment, and Haynes International and VDM Metals for nickel-based alloys in the alloy segment; market shares are not stated, and the filing says competition and excess capacity have at times reduced prices excluding surcharges. Rivalry therefore caps pricing power in industrial markets but is less of a threat to margin in qualified aerospace products.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 18

The threat of new entrants is low in aerospace because fulfilling contracts requires meeting exacting performance requirements and product specifications, and the company's melt, forging, finishing and machining integration is hard to copy quickly; the threat is higher in industrial flat products. Substitutes matter mainly in industrial markets, where the filing cites lower-priced imports and substitute materials. Both forces protect margin in the engine-component segment and leave the alloy segment's industrial sales more exposed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 17

Buyer power is high in structure and moderated in practice: a small number of engine and airframe makers dominate demand, but no customer exceeded 10% of sales, long-term agreements are in place with most of them, and some are subject to renewal, renegotiation or re-pricing. Supplier power is limited for most inputs, which are available from more than one supplier, but nickel, titanium sponge, cobalt and ferrochromium come mostly from foreign sources that may face unstable conditions, and some supply arrangements rely on a limited number of suppliers, so supply or price shocks reach margin before surcharges reset.
### PEST analysis

Political and regulatory factors are material: international sales were about 42% of FY2025 sales, 37% of 9M 2026 sales against 42% a year earlier, and the annual report says changes in trade policy could raise the cost of imported raw materials such as nickel and titanium sponge and of exported products. Economic factors are the main driver, through the commercial aerospace and industrial cycles described above. Technological change matters in that a new nickel-based superalloy entering production already dilutes the engine-component margin. Social factors matter through labour terms, with about 35% of the workforce under collective agreements, but they are not a primary credit driver.
### SWOT analysis

Strengths are leverage that has fallen to 1.92x total and 1.46x net on reported EBITDA, liquidity that covers the next senior note maturity 3.11 times, and contracts and orders that cover about a year. Weaknesses are shareholder returns above free cash flow, concentration in aerospace and defense, and USD 203.0 million of funding outside reported debt. Opportunities are the growth in commercial jet engine and defense demand reflected in a USD 4.3 billion backlog, and capacity projects that can lift volume without new debt if funded from cash flow. Threats are a cut in engine build rates, trade-policy and input cost shocks that arrive before surcharges, and buybacks funded by borrowing.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next year or two the tailwinds are the order book of about USD 4.3 billion, price and mix gains, defense and specialty energy growth in the alloy segment, and a refinancing that has removed nearby maturities; these support revenue, margin and cash-flow visibility. The headwinds are superalloy ramp costs, inventory build, tariff and input cost exposure and payouts above free cash flow, which pressure margin, free cash flow and deleveraging. Over three to five years the credit depends on whether the earnings step-up lasts through the FY2029 and FY2030 maturities of USD 325.0 million of senior notes and USD 633.4 million in the largest ladder year, and on whether the company keeps returns within free cash flow as capacity growth ends.

### Qualitative downside scenario

The realistic downside starts with a cut in commercial engine build rates or a trade shock that raises nickel and titanium costs ahead of surcharges. The first operating break is lower engine-component volume and a margin squeeze from fixed labour and superalloy ramp costs, with inventories, already up USD 255.1 million in 9M 2026, slow to unwind. Because EBITDA grew 22.75% on revenue growth of 9.29%, a reversal would cut EBITDA faster than revenue: at the FY2025 level of USD 789.0 million, with debt unchanged, total debt over EBITDA would be 2.35x and net debt 1.79x, and at the FY2024 level of USD 745.8 million, 2.49x and 1.90x. Cash flow would fall with EBITDA, and if buybacks continued free cash flow would again sit below returns. Management can slow growth capex, stop buybacks, which are discretionary, and release inventory. Liquidity of USD 1,012.3 million would still cover the USD 325.0 million FY2029 maturity 3.11 times, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, but leverage would return to the levels of FY2024 and FY2025 and refinancing in FY2029 and FY2030 would be harder if the market had turned. The signals to watch are orders, the Adjusted EBITDA margin, free cash flow against returns and availability under the revolver.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C1
### Overall credit view

Overall, Ati Inc presents an adequate business profile supported by qualified aerospace products, contract cover for about a year and USD 1,012.3 million of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by shareholder returns above free cash flow, concentration in the aerospace cycle and USD 203.0 million of funding outside reported debt. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: free cash flow is positive in every period but absorbs growth investment, and free cash flow after returns was negative in 9M 2026. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding earnings through FY2029 and FY2030, when USD 325.0 million of senior notes and the largest ladder year of USD 633.4 million fall due. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector the profile cannot be placed because peer data is not supplied. The primary downside path is a fall in engine build rates while buybacks continue, which would lift leverage back toward 2.35x. Further analysis would require agency ratings, the executed credit agreement and indentures, peer data and the proxy statement. Top risk: earnings concentrated in the commercial aerospace cycle combined with shareholder returns above free cash flow.
